title: Atmosphere comparison: air versus 30 % O2 / He
summary: Same fuel and stoichiometry, two oxidizer mixtures. Step A: run in dry air. Step B: press "Variant B" (30 % O2 in helium) and run again. The equilibrium state is recomputed by Cantera each time.
expected_behaviour: The helium-diluted, oxygen-enriched mixture gives a higher adiabatic flame temperature than air because He has a lower molar heat capacity than N2 and more O2 is available per mole of diluent.
acceptance_checks: Both runs complete with element-balance residual below 1e-9.
Adiabatic temperature in air is 2225 K +/- 15 K (CH4, phi = 1, 300 K, 1 atm, GRI-Mech 3.0).
Variant B temperature is higher than variant A.

variants.label: Variant A: dry air (21 % O2 / 79 % N2)
